title: A Complete Test File
description: The full test_mylang.py, grouped into classes by feature: arithmetic, booleans, variables, functions, recursion, errors, and lexer-level isolation.

steps.description: This is the complete test file, `tests/test_mylang.py`. It imports `pytest`, `run`, `tokenize`, and `parse` from `mylang`, and the error classes from the lexer, parser, and evaluator. The page says it covers the core features of the Mini interpreter from class.
`TestArithmetic` covers integer and negative literals, the four operators, operator precedence, left associativity, and parentheses. Two comments spell out the precedence and associativity cases.

`TestBooleans` covers the `true` and `false` literals, equality, less-than and greater-than, and the two `if` branches, including a condition that is itself an expression. `TestVariables` covers `let` bindings, nested `let`, shadowing, and the outer binding restored after a shadow, and checks that an undefined variable raises `LangNameError`.

`TestFunctions` covers identity, a constant function, a function that uses its argument, curried addition, closures that capture an outer variable, a higher-order function, and a function returned from a function.

`TestRecursion` covers the factorial base case and `fact 5`, plus Fibonacci. The mutual-recursion test is skipped with a message, because the page says it needs a feature your interpreter may not have yet.

`TestErrors` covers a `LexError` on an unknown character, two `ParseError` cases, two `LangTypeError` cases, and a `LangNameError` in a function body. `TestLexer` tests stage isolation: a token's type and value, keyword recognition, the EOF token, and the empty-source case.
